title: Quant Compatibility Scrape - weekly capture
body:
Week of 2028-01-15 — quick capture / working notes

Context / goal:
- Scrape and summarise compatibility issues surfaced during the last two onboarding attempts for 7B-class open models when applying 4-bit and 8-bit post-training quantization (PTQ) with our compact kernels. Focus on functional parity (sampler diffs), KV-cache correctness, and perf regressions at tail latency.
- Produce a short list of blockers + next triage steps for the rollout task on the private fleet and Dedicated pools.

Attendees (standup 2028-01-16):
- Avery Martinez (owner)
- Liam Chen (bench + kernels)
- Sofia Patel (evals + metrics)
- Noah Kim (onboarding automation)
- Elena Rodriguez (SRE / perf observability)

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Two recurring classes of failure for 4-bit PTQ: (1) KV-cache misalignment when resuming generation after streaming fallback, resulting in token duplication on long context (>2048 tokens). Repro rate ~18% on our test set. (2) Numerics near softmax causing hallucinated stop tokens in a few samples for one model variant (cause: reduced mantissa precision interacting with fused attention kernel).
- 8-bit asymmetric quant passes functional checks more reliably but shows 12–18% tail latency uplift on small batch sizes due to additional dequant ops in the critical path on older GPUs.
- Patch in PR #2784 reduces KV-cache mismatch by ~60% in internal microbench but uncovered a race in the streaming path.

Notes / observations:
- Repro harness used: eval-runner v0.42 (local), with seedset=prod-evals/seqset-1200, prompts padded to 3 different lengths (256, 1024, 3072). Baseline model: redwood-xenon-7b-v1 (non-quantized). Variants: xenon-7b-q4f, xenon-7b-q8a.
- Failure mode A (KV misalignment): happens on resumed calls after a streaming fallback where the runtime attaches a prefix cache that was generated under fp16 but is reused with q4 runtime path. Root cause hypothesis: cache key ordering or per-layer buffer stride mismatch when switching execution kernels. Liam found an off-by-one in chunk_size calculation in the kernel selector.
- Failure mode B (softmax instability): present mostly on samples with many punctuation tokens; numeric differences between fp16 and q4 propagate to top-k token differences early and cascade. Sofia's diffs show >0.5 perplexity jump on ~7% of the seedset for q4 on model-variant-2.
- Latency: p50 unchanged, but p95/p99 increase observed for q8a on older V100 machines in our dedicated fleet. Elena traced this to an extra copy/dequant on host due to missing fused path for an older CUDA version.

Quick metrics (aggregate from 2028-01-14 to 2028-01-18 runs):
- Functional parity pass rate (exact-token match at 512 steps): q4: 78%; q8: 91% (baseline 100%).
- KV-mismatch repro rate (samples with duplicated tokens after resume): q4: 18% (reduced to 7% with local PR patch), q8: 3%.
- Eval delta (avg logprob / BLEU-esque proxy): q4: -0.24 (stat sig), q8: -0.06 (small).
- Tail latency delta (p99): q8 on V100 +12–18%; q4 on A100 negligible change.

Experiment log (short):
- 2028-01-15 a.m. — ran corpus sweep w/ chunk_size variants (8, 16, 32) — chunk_size=16 reduced mismatch incidence by ~40% but didn't eliminate it. Related to kernel selector change. (Liam)
- 2028-01-15 p.m. — quick test of alternative quant-zero-point handling for q8a: improved softmax stability slightly (Sofia).
- 2028-01-16 — merged microbench patch (PR #2784) to mainline for internal bench; required hotfix in streaming adapter (WIP).
- 2028-01-17 — stress run on private fleet (low-load): q4 fallback triggered ~1/500 requests; reproduced KV duplication under a specific resume sequence. Noah captured logs and stored in /artifacts/kv-resume-logs/kv-jan17.tar.gz (link in Confluence).

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Is the mismatch a kernel selector bug (stride/offset) or an upstream buffer management issue from the serving runtime?
- Does a small per-layer dequantization at the resume boundary (convert cache to fp16 on resume and then re-quantize) reduce the repro while preserving cost? (tradeoff: extra CPU/GPU cycles at resume)
- Are there particular token/token-pos patterns that increase the chance of softmax cascades when quantized? Could be tied to fixed vocab embeddings and certain punctuation-heavy prompts.

Immediate action items (owner — due):
- Add a focused unit test: simulate streaming fallback -> resume across kernel-switch boundary with synthetic cache states. (Liam — 2028-01-21)
- Instrument kernel selector to emit chosen stride/format per layer for the failing runs and add to eval-runner logs. (Liam, Noah — 2028-01-20)
- Run per-token stability analysis across seedset to find tokens that correlate with high diff cascades (Sofia — 2028-01-22)
- Prototype resume-boundary dequant/quant conversion in a feature branch and run perf vs correctness sweep. (Noah — 2028-01-25)
- Add an emergency rollback flag in rollout config so Dedicated pools can opt out of q4 variants if mismatch rate > 5% for 24h. (Avery / Platform — 2028-01-19)
- SRE: ensure p99 latency alerting includes quant-variant labels (Elena — 2028-01-20)

Notes to self / brainstorming (fast, rough):
- Maybe implement a cheap checksum of KV per-layer that travels with streaming fragments — quick mismatch detection + failover to fp16 path. Lightweight, could help auto-failover before duplication is observed in user output.
- Consider adding a small-scale QAT with a handful of calibration batches for the punctuation-heavy subset. Might reduce softmax sensitivity more effectively than PTQ tweaks. Costly, but could be targeted for a few problematic variants.

Docs / docs TODOs:
- Update quant-onboarding playbook checklist to include: resume-scenario test, per-layer stride logging, and tagged eval reports for punctuation-heavy prompts. (Noah — 2028-01-20)
- Add short note to rollout runbook about how to use the emergency rollback flag and how to interpret the KV-checksum if implemented. (Avery — 2028-01-23)

Follow-ups for next weekly sync (2028-01-23):
- Demo of unit test reproducer + failing logs (Liam)
- Results from per-token stability scan + candidate token blacklist/targeted QAT plan (Sofia)
- Prototype resume-boundary conversion perf numbers (Noah)
- Decision on whether q4 variants remain enabled for private fleet incremental rollout (Avery + Platform)

Random scratch / links:
- Quick grep output showing duplicated token pattern: "the the" consistent pattern in resume case (attached to PR comments).
- Local microbench command used: eval-runner --seedset prod-evals/seqset-1200 --variants xenon-7b-v1,xenon-7b-q4f,xenon-7b-q8a --record-kv-checksums

End of capture. This doc is a working log — will iterate as tests complete and we decide on a rollout posture.
summary: Working weekly notes capturing quantization compatibility issues (KV-cache misalignment and softmax instability), metrics from recent sweeps, experiment log, and concrete action items for kernel selection fixes, instrumentation, and a potential resume-boundary dequant prototype.
